title: India Opens CWG 2026 With Two Lawn Bowls Wins Despite Doping Cloud Over Glasgow Campaign
excerpt: Putul Sonowal and the women's pairs team clinch tie-breaker victories on Day 1 in Glasgow, but four weightlifting doping cases have already dented India's medal prospects at the pared-down Commonwealth Games.
body:
• Putul Sonowal and the women's pairs duo of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki won their opening lawn bowls matches via tie-breakers at Emirates Arena in Glasgow
  • Four Indian weightlifters tested positive for banned substances ahead of the Games, reducing medal chances in a traditionally dominant discipline
  • India's 126-member contingent faces the leanest Commonwealth Games in three decades, with key medal sports like wrestling, badminton and hockey dropped from the programme

India's 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign got off to a winning start in Glasgow on Thursday, as lawn bowlers secured victories in both their opening matches at the Emirates Arena — hours before the opening ceremony officially inaugurated the Games at the OVO Hydro.

Putul Sonowal, making his Commonwealth Games debut, edged past Canada's Ryan Bester in the men's singles Section D match, winning via a tie-breaker after the two shared sets 1-1. The result was particularly noteworthy given Sonowal trailed on overall shot count 8-11, but the 2026 Asian Lawn Bowls Championship gold medallist held his nerve in the decider.

In the women's pairs, Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki — both part of India's historic women's fours gold medal-winning team at Birmingham 2022 — defeated Malta's Connie Rixon and Rebecca Rixon in Section B. The Indian pair dominated the shot count 10-5 but still needed a tie-breaker to clinch the match point.

"India's lawn bowls story took off at Birmingham 2022. Several of those medal winners are back for Glasgow 2026."

— World Bowls, pre-Games preview

Doping blow weakens weightlifting squad

The early lawn bowls results offered welcome relief for an Indian contingent that arrived in Glasgow under a cloud. Four weightlifters — N Ajith (71kg), Sairaj Pardeshi (88kg), Harcharan Singh (110kg) and Vanshita Verma (77kg) — were dropped from the squad after testing positive for prohibited substances during the national selection camp, according to Bhasha Times.

Ajith and Pardeshi were considered strong gold-medal contenders, and their absence has significantly weakened India's prospects in a discipline that has traditionally been its richest medal-winning hunting ground at the Commonwealth Games.

The setback comes after India was re-classified by the Athletics Integrity Unit as a Category A federation — the highest-risk tier — following a rise in doping violations across Indian sport. Under the enhanced framework, Indian athletes must now complete three out-of-competition tests within 10 months before major competitions.

"The rule is very clear that countries categorised in Category A are subject to enhanced testing. This is not something introduced specifically for Glasgow."

— Adille Sumariwalla, World Athletics vice-president, speaking to RevSportz

A leaner Games, a tougher test

India's 126-member contingent faces the most challenging Commonwealth Games in recent memory. After Victoria withdrew as host, Glasgow stepped in with a programme slashed to just 10 sports — down from 19 at Birmingham 2022.

Wrestling, badminton, hockey, shooting, table tennis and cricket have all been dropped. Those sports collectively delivered 25 of India's 61 medals four years ago, including 13 of 22 gold medals. The reduced programme means India will lean heavily on athletics, boxing, weightlifting and lawn bowls for its medal haul.

Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra leads the 32-member athletics squad, with the men's javelin throw final set for August 1. Two-time Commonwealth champion Mirabai Chanu, who carried India's flag at Thursday's opening ceremony alongside baton bearer Lovlina Borgohain, remains the country's safest gold-medal prospect in weightlifting despite the reduced squad.

Looking ahead

Competition ramps up quickly. Lawn bowls continues through the weekend — Sonowal faces Kenya next, while the women's pairs take on South Africa. Boxing begins on July 25, artistic gymnastics qualifications start on July 26, and the marquee athletics programme runs from July 27 to August 1 at Scotstoun Stadium.

The opening ceremony at the OVO Hydro — headlined by Scottish singer-songwriter KT Tunstall and attended by the King and Queen — marked the first time the event has been staged entirely indoors. With that pageantry behind them, India's athletes will need to convert every available opportunity if the country is to extend its streak of top-five finishes at the Commonwealth Games, a run unbroken since Manchester 2002.
